sentences.text:
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of the M.V.Act 1989.
2.

The brief facts of case of the Petitioner is that:
The petitioner being minor represented by mother and natural guardian.

That on 05.02.2023 at about 11.30 a.m. petitioner had been drinking tender coconut along with her father near Yellamma Temple, Chunchagatta Main Road, Bengaluru, at that time, a driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-36-C-1732 came SCCH-5 at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against heap of tender coconuts, due to the said impact, tender coconuts were fell on the petitioner, as a result she fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was taken to Supra Hospital, thereafter shifted to Aster R.V.Hospital, wherein she took treatment as indoor patient, for which, her father had spent Rs.10,00,000/- for hospitalization,
treatment, transportation, medicines and nourishment.

3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 3 years and student, due to the said accident, she is unable to do her basic work and depending on her parents for her routine work and her parents have to look after her by sacrificing their work.

Out of the said accident, crime No.47/2023 is registered before the Kumaraswamy Layout P.S. for the offences punishable SCCH-5 under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC against the driver of the said tractor.
Respondent is the owner of the tractor is liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- along with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, mother and natural guardian of the petitioner is examined as PW-1, examined Deputy Manager of Aster R.V.Hospital as PW-2 and Dr. Avinash Parthasarathy as PW-3 and marked 24 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.24 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondent remained absent, hence there is no evidence of respondent.
SCCH-5 6.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record,
7.

On going through the pleadings of the parties, the points that would arise for my consideration:
::POINTS::
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, She has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 05.02.2023 at about 11.30 a.m. near Yallamma Temple Chunchagatta Main Road, Bengaluru while drinking tender coconut, at that time, tractor bearing Reg.No. KA-36-C- 732 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the tender coconuts, as a result of which,
Dhrithi Nitin Savanur vs Amaresh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118041700/
2 coconut fell down on the petitioner and sustained grievous injurie, as mentioned in claim petition?

3. What order or award?
SCCH-5 8.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
9. Point No.1:-
In order to prove the above point, the mother and natural guardian of the Petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW-1 by way of reiterating the facts narrated in the petition.
Hence, in order to avoid the repetition of facts, chief- examination of the PW-1 is not reproduced here.

In support of her case, PW-1 has furnished copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of charge sheet marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.5, SCCH-5 copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.9.
10.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and records, which corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 05.02.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, inspite of service of notice, respondent has not appeared before the court and even not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 05.02.2023 at about 11.30 a.m. while she was drinking tender coconut SCCH-5 along with her father near Yallamma Temple, Chunchagatta Main Road, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the tractor driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the PW-1,
this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Point No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: 13. Point No.2:-
As per the case of the Petitioner, she was aged about 3 years as on the date of accident.

In order to prove her age, PW-1 has produced copy of aadhar card of the petitioner marked as Ex.P.17, wherein SCCH-5 date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 29.08.2020, the alleged accident is occurred on 05.02.2023.
Relying on Ex.P.17 this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner at 3 years as on the date of accident.
14. It is the case of the petitioner that, she has sustained fracture shaft of right femur, moderate head injury, for which she underwent CRIF application for femur fracture.

In this regard, PW-1 has produced copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.10, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.11 issued by Aster RV Hospital wherein she took treatment as indoor patient since 05.02.2023 to 11.02.2023.

Further PW-1 has produced medical bills of Rs.5,59,026/- marked as Ex.P.12,
invoice-cum-receipts marked as Ex.P.13, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.14, test reports marked as SCCH-5 Ex.P.15, X-ray Films and MRI Scan are marked as Ex.P.16.

15 . In support of her case, Deputy Manager in Aster RV Hospital is examined as PW-2 who has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.18, copy of MLC Extract marked as Ex.P.19, copy of Police Intimation marked as Ex.P.20 and case sheet is marked as Ex.P.21.

Further Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy, Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sreenivasa Hospital is examined as PW-3 and furnished recent OPD Slip marked as Ex.P.22, assessment report marked as Ex.P.23 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.24.
PW-3 has assessed PPI in right lower limb at the rate of 30% and whole body disability at the rate of 10%.
So considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, functional disability is taken at the rate of 10%.
SCCH-5 16.

sentences.text: For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Re.1 lakh".
17. So herein this case, permanent disability is upto 10% is caused to the minor child as per the Doctor evidence.
Hence, loss of future income shall be awarded at the rate of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Accordingly petitioner is SCCH-5 entitled for loss of future income of Rs.1,00,000/- along with other heads.

18. Further she is entitled for Rs.15,000/- for pain and sufferings, Rs.15,000/- for inconvenience caused to her parents, loss of future amenities of Rs.15,000/-, conveyance food and nourishment charges of Rs.15,000/-.
PW-1 has has produced medical bills to the tune of Rs.5,59,026/- marked as Ex.P.12.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,04,026/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
21. The respondent is the owner of the tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-36-C-1732 and the said vehicle does not possessed valid insurance as on the date of accident.
So that, respondent is liable to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Point No.2 partly in the affirmative.
22. Point No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
SCCH-5 The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,04,026/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Four Thousand Twenty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount, The Respondent shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

On deposit of compensation amount, PW-1 i.e., mother and natural guardian of the petitioner is entitled to get release 50% of the award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.

Remaining 50% ordered to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank in the name of minor Petitioner till she attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioner.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
